proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an enumerated architecture \(T\) and a point \(p_T\) of its product of source simplexes.  All source masses are nonnegative.  For a directed-feature index \(e=\operatorname{dir}(i,j)\), the definition of \(Z_e\) gives a finite expansion
\[
 Z_e(T,p_T)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X_e} I_e(x)w_{p_T}(x),
 \qquad I_e(x)\in\{0,1\},\qquad w_{p_T}(x)\ge 0,
\]
where \(x\) specifies an exogenous response context, \(w_{p_T}(x)\) is the product of the corresponding source masses, and \(I_e(x)=1\) precisely when two assignments of the endogenous inputs of the table for \(j\), differing only at \(i\), give different outputs.  This comparison ranges over all endogenous input assignments by the definition of the graph-legality stratum; it is not restricted to naturally observed inputs.

Because the sum is finite and every summand is nonnegative,
\[
 Z_e(T,p_T)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists x\in\mathcal X_e:\ I_e(x)=1\ \text{ and }\ w_{p_T}(x)>0.
\]
The condition \(w_{p_T}(x)>0\) says exactly that the displayed exogenous context is outside an exogenous null set.  The right-hand side is therefore the definition of actual functional dependence of the equation for \(j\) on \(i\), with all endogenous inputs available for the comparison.  By the definition of \(G_S\), this is equivalent to the presence of \(i\to j\) in the minimal structural graph.

For \(e=\operatorname{src}(C,j)\), the same argument is applied to the expansion
\[
 Z_e(T,p_T)=
 \sum_{(u,u',x)\in\mathcal Y_e}
 J_e(u,u',x),p_C(u)p_C(u')w_{-C,p_T}(x).
\]
Here \(J_e(u,u',x)=1\) exactly when, at the same endogenous input and the same other-source context \(x\), the table for \(j\) differs between the two values \(u,u'\) of \(U_C\).  Again every term is nonnegative.  Thus \(Z_e>0\) if and only if there are two positive-mass source values and a positive-probability other-source context witnessing that dependence.  This is precisely that \(U_C\) is an actual parent of \(j\).  Notice that the factors \(p_C(u)p_C(u')\) exclude witnesses supported only at zero-mass source values.

Consequently the signs \(Z_e>0\) and equalities \(Z_e=0\), for \(e\in\mathcal I_T\), recover every primitive edge of the minimal structural graph and no nonexistent edge.  Latent projection followed by selected-MAG projection is a deterministic finite graph operation.  The definition of \(\Psi_{T,G}\) therefore yields
\[
 G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Psi_{T,G}(p_T).
\]
Finally, a permutation of source values, response-table labels, or equally indexed sources merely bijects the summation indices above and leaves every zero or strict-positive test unchanged.  The canonical child-set index \(C\) and the projected graph are consequently invariant under all three kinds of relabeling.  This proves the lemma.

We prove the three assertions separately.

First, group the mutually independent exogenous sources of a recursive SCM according to their nonempty sets of retained children.  For each \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq W\), let \(U_C\) be the tuple of all original sources having retained child set \(C\), with the product law inherited from those sources.  Tuples associated with distinct child sets use disjoint original coordinates and hence remain mutually independent.  Substitute the tuple coordinates into the old structural equations.  For every joint exogenous realization and every intervention, the new recursive evaluation is then identical, node by node in topological order, to the old evaluation.  Thus all structural solutions, including \((V,S)\) and \((A^b,S^b)\), are unchanged.  A retained equation depends essentially on the tuple \(U_C\) exactly when it depends essentially on at least one of its coordinates: the reverse implication follows by changing that coordinate, and the forward implication follows by changing two tuples one coordinate at a time and taking the first step at which the output changes.  Hence this merging does not change the minimal structural graph.  Empty-child sources may be discarded.  There are exactly \(2^N-1=H_{\max}\) nonempty subsets of \(W\), proving the source-count bound.

Second, fix one permitted architecture with independent sources \(U_1,\ldots,U_H\), where \(H\le H_{\max}\).  Define the bounded vector
\[
 F(U_1,\ldots,U_H)=
 \left(
   (\mathbf 1\{V=v,S=1\})_{v\in\Omega_V},
   h(A^b)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\},
   \mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}
 \right)\in\mathbb R^{m+2}.
\]
Its expectation is \(\zeta(M)\) by the moment-map definition.  Hold all source laws except that of \(U_k\) fixed and put
\[
 g_k(u)=\int F(u_1,\ldots,u_{k-1},u,u_{k+1},\ldots,u_H)
              \prod_{r\ne k}dP_r(u_r).
\]
Then independence and iterated integration give
\[
 \zeta(M)=\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]
We use the following elementary finite-dimensional barycenter fact.  If a probability law has an integrable image in \(\mathbb R^d\), its barycenter is a convex combination of at most \(d+1\) values of that image.  To verify the fact, take the smallest face of the closed convex hull of the essential image that contains the barycenter.  Every supporting affine functional of that face is equal to its value at the barycenter almost surely, because its one-sided nonnegative difference has integral zero.  The barycenter is therefore in the relative interior of the convex hull of the image inside that face.  Successively removing affine dependencies from any finite convex representation leaves at most \(d+1\) image points without changing the barycenter.  This also shows that actual image values, rather than merely closure points, may be used.

Apply the fact with \(d=m+2\).  There are values \(u_{k,1},\ldots,u_{k,L_k}\), weights \(w_{k,r}\ge0\), and \(L_k\le m+3=K_{\max}\) such that
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}g_k(u_{k,r})
   =\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]
Replacing only \(P_k\) by this discrete law leaves \(\zeta(M)\) unchanged and retains product factorization.  Repeat this operation for \(k=1,\ldots,H\), each time using the currently installed laws for the other sources.  Every step preserves the same full vector, so the final vector is still \(\zeta(M)\), and every source has at most \(K_{\max}\) values.  In particular,
\[
 \rho=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}c_v(M)
\]
is preserved with the common normalization; no separately scaled normalized cells have been substituted.  Since the retained state spaces and all reduced source supports are finite, every structural equation is one of the deterministic response tables counted in \(R_{\max}\).  This argument preserves moments on the permitted slots.  It does not prove that strict essential-feature inequalities survive the replacement.

Third, take \((p_T,\rho)\in\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  The topological order in \(T\), its deterministic tables, and the mutually independent source simplexes define a recursive finite SCM \(M_{T,p_T}\).  By the exact graph-legality constraint and the essential-feature lemma, there is a \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) for which
\[
 G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G.
\]
The remaining defining constraints of the finite legal fiber give, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 c_v(M_{T,p_T})=\Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v),\qquad
 \delta\le\rho\le1,
 \qquad
 d_{M_{T,p_T}}=\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta.
\]
Together with the positive-law assumption, these are exactly the five member conditions in the admissible-class definition.  Hence \(M_{T,p_T}\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\), and division in \(\theta(M_{T,p_T})=\Phi_T(p_T)_n/\Phi_T(p_T)_d\) is valid because \(\delta>0\).

Conversely, every enumerated bounded finite SCM satisfying actual selected-MAG legality has a listed topological architecture, a listed deterministic table system, product source masses \(p_T\), and \(\rho=\sum_vc_v\).  Its selected-law fit and both margin restrictions place \((p_T,\rho)\) in \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\), while the essential-feature lemma selects its exact graph branch.  The two inclusions prove that the image of the finite legal fiber is exactly the target-value set of the enumerated bounded legal SCMs.  Neither inclusion asserts that the preceding barycentric replacement of an arbitrary admissible SCM is itself legal, nor that every arbitrary admissible SCM already has a representative in this bounded union.

Fix a labeled source architecture and a deterministic response-table system.  Write its \(H\) source-mass vectors as \(p_1,\ldots,p_H\).  For each coordinate \(y\) of the moment map there are rational table coefficients \(a_y(u_1,\ldots,u_H)\) such that
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_y
 =\sum_{u_1,\ldots,u_H}
   a_y(u_1,\ldots,u_H)\prod_{k=1}^H p_k(u_k).
\]
For a cell coordinate or \(d\), the coefficient is zero or one; for \(n\), it is a value of \(h\) or zero.  Thus the moment coordinates are rational polynomials of degree at most \(H\).  By the essential-feature lemma, each directed-feature test is the sign of a nonnegative polynomial of degree at most \(H\), and a source-feature test uses two copies of one source mass and has degree at most \(H+1\).  The simplex equations and inequalities, the equalities \(\Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v)\), the two bounds on \(\rho\), and \(\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta\) are therefore a finite Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions with rational coefficients.  Rationality uses the declared rationality of \(q\), \(\delta\), and \(h\).

Introduce \(t\) and add
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_n-t\Phi_T(p_T)_d=0.
\]
The strict and weak feature conditions in \(\Psi_{T,G}\) are retained, so existential projection of this formula is exactly the branch of \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\), not its closure.  There are at most
\[
 A_{\max}=N!\,2^{N(N-1)/2+2^N-1}
\]
labeled architectures: choose a vertex order, forward directed slots, and nonempty source child sets.  For each architecture, the response-table count is at most \(R_{\max}\) by direct multiplication over the finitely many input configurations in the definition of that bound.

For completeness, we spell out the real-algebraic decision step used by the procedure.  Given finitely many integer polynomials after clearing denominators, recursively form their coefficients in the last variable, discriminants, and pairwise resultants.  On every cell on which all projection polynomials have constant sign, no leading coefficient vanishes unexpectedly, no two real roots cross, and no root changes multiplicity.  Isolating the real roots in one variable by signed remainder sequences gives the base decomposition; lifting the isolated roots and intervening sectors gives, inductively, a finite cylindrical decomposition on which every input polynomial has constant sign.  Consequently the truth of each quantified conjunction is constant on every cell.  Checking the sample point of every cell decides its existential quantifier and then every finite disjunction.  All sample coordinates are obtained by adjoining isolated real roots to rational or previously algebraic coordinates, and hence are real algebraic.

Applying this construction first decides whether any branch of \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) is nonempty.  If none is, the output is INFEASIBLE.  Otherwise elimination of the response parameters leaves a quantifier-free one-variable sign formula for the attainable \(t\)'s.  Because \(h_-\le h(A^b)\le h_+\) pointwise and \(d\ge\delta>0\),
\[
 h_-d\le n\le h_+d,
 \qquad
 h_-\le t=\frac nd\le h_+.
\]
The nonempty projected set is therefore bounded.  Its boundary points occur among the finitely many real roots of the univariate projection polynomials, so its infimum and supremum are real algebraic and are isolated exactly by signed remainder sequences.

At either isolated endpoint \(t_0\), rerun the sign test with \(t=t_0\).  If \(\mathsf{Lift}(t_0)\) is true, a sample point of a satisfying lifted cell provides algebraic values of \(p_T\) and \(\rho\); the finitely many coordinates can equivalently be encoded by a primitive element and rational univariate representation.  Its signs satisfy \(\Psi_{T,G}\), and the essential-feature lemma verifies the actual graph.  If \(\mathsf{Lift}(t_0)\) is false, retain the finite sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition for every \((T,G)\) branch.  Every cell either violates a simplex or moment constraint, violates the required sign pattern, or violates the endpoint equation.  These finitely many cell checks cover the whole response-parameter space and therefore certify that no enumerated legal lift exists.

It remains to justify the displayed elementary complexity form.  At one projection step, coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants increase the number and degrees of polynomials by at most a fixed polynomial in the current number and degree.  If \(s_k,D_k\) denote these quantities with \(k\) variables remaining, the resultant determinant formula gives bounds of the form
\[
 s_{k-1}D_{k-1}\le (s_kD_k)^{C}
\]
after enlarging the absolute constant \(C\); iterating the projection and lifting recurrences, including root isolation at every level, gives
\[
 (s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{,2^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}}
 \operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}})
\]
arithmetic and expanded-coefficient work per table branch.  The coefficient length here is explicitly the length after the rational formulas have been expanded, so no hidden succinct-circuit claim is being made.  Multiplying by the at most \(A_{\max}R_{\max}\) enumerated branches proves the stated bound and all certificate claims.

Assume the affirmative universal legal-lifting property posed in the open-ended question.  Let \(\mathcal Z_b\) be the set of moment vectors \(\zeta(M_{T,p_T})\) represented by the bounded finite legal fiber, including the constraints \(c_v=\rho q(v)\), \(\delta\le\rho\le1\), and \(d\ge\delta\).  It is bounded because each cell coordinate and \(d\) lies in \([0,1]\), while
\[
 |n|\le \max\{|h_-|,|h_+|\}d\le \max\{|h_-|,|h_+|\}.
\]

We next prove closedness, which does not follow merely from the strict graph-legality inequalities.  Let \(z_r\in\mathcal Z_b\) and \(z_r\to z\).  The second half of the assumed lifting property supplies a finite SCM with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) and moment vector \(z\).  The equalities and weak inequalities defining selected-law fit and both margins pass to the limit.  In particular, because \(q\) is a probability mass function,
\[
 \rho_r=\sum_v(z_r)_{c_v}\longrightarrow
 \rho=\sum_vz_{c_v}\in[\delta,1],
 \qquad z_{c_v}=\rho q(v),
 \qquad z_d\ge\delta.
\]
This finite legal SCM is admissible.  The first half of the assumed lifting property then gives an equal-moment representative in the bounded finite legal fiber, so \(z\in\mathcal Z_b\).  Hence \(\mathcal Z_b\) is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and therefore compact.

By the first half of the lifting property, the full admissible moment set equals \(\mathcal Z_b\).  On this set the map \((c,n,d)\mapsto n/d\) is continuous because \(d\ge\delta>0\).  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)
 =\left\{\frac nd:(c,n,d)\in\mathcal Z_b\right\}
\]
is compact whenever it is nonempty.  Moreover, each architecture branch is described by finitely many rational polynomial equalities and strict or weak inequalities, and there are finitely many branches.  The elimination construction in the certified-procedure theorem projects their finite union to a quantifier-free univariate polynomial sign formula.  Thus \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) is semialgebraic.  Sorting the finitely many real roots of the polynomials in that formula partitions the real line into finitely many points and open intervals on each of which membership is constant.  Compactness closes every included endpoint.  Hence the fiber is a finite union of closed intervals and points contained in \([h_-,h_+]\).

The same root partition shows that every finite endpoint is algebraic because all input coefficients are rational.  Compactness makes the outer endpoints \(\ell\) and \(u\) members of the fiber.  At either endpoint, \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) is true, so the positive certificate in the certified-procedure theorem supplies algebraic source probabilities and a finite response-SCM witness.

Finally we count a branch.  With the last mass of each source eliminated by normalization, \(H\) sources of support at most \(K\) require \(H(K-1)\) mass parameters; adding \(\rho\) and the endpoint coordinate changes this only by two.  Thus
\[
 p_{\mathrm{dim}}=O(H_{\max}K_{\max}).
\]
There are \(O(HK)\) simplex sign conditions, \(m\) selected-cell equations, a constant number of margin and endpoint conditions, \(O(N^2)\) directed-feature tests, and at most
\[
 \sum_{U_C\text{ present}}|C|\le NH
\]
source-child feature tests.  The finite graph projection may be precomputed, and a conservative bookkeeping allowance of \(O(N^3)\) covers its finite adjacency and orientation checks.  Consequently the valid uniform count is
\[
 s_{\mathrm{count}}
 =O\!\left(m+H_{\max}K_{\max}+NH_{\max}+N^3\right).
\]
Moment polynomials have degree at most \(H\); a source-essentiality polynomial and the endpoint equation have degree at most \(H+1\).  The advertised conservative form \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}=O(H_{\max}+N)\) follows.  Substitution of these quantities into the per-architecture bound proved by the certified procedure yields
\[
 (s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{2^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}}
 \operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}).
\]
This proves the corrected conditional theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If the universal legal-lifting property in Open-ended Question 1 holds, then every nonempty \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \([h_-,h_+]\), hence a finite union of closed intervals and points; \(\ell\) and \(u\) are attained algebraic numbers and admit finite response-SCM witnesses. With \(H_{\max}=2^N-1\), source support bounded by \(K_{\max}=m+3\), parameter count \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}=O(H_{\max}K_{\max})\), constraint count \(s_{\mathrm{count}}=O(m+H_{\max}K_{\max}+NH_{\max}+N^3)\), degree \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}=O(H_{\max}+N)\), and expanded coefficient bit length \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\), cylindrical algebraic decomposition gives the per-architecture factor \((s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{2^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}}\operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}})\) in the certified procedure.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current count omits the exact source-child essentiality tests. An architecture may contain \(H_{\max}\) child-set sources and requires as many as \(NH_{\max}\) source-child sign tests. Without an assumption relating \(N\) to \(m\), this term is not uniformly absorbed by \(H_{\max}K_{\max}+N^3\). The proposed claim changes only this complexity upper bound and is therefore an honest narrowing.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law \(q\), prove or refute that every arbitrary admissible moment vector and every limit of bounded exact-graph moment vectors has an equal-moment representative in the bounded fiber with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The selected cell and intervention moments are linear in each source law separately, but a source-essentiality witness \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}\) is quadratic in the law of its own source. Ordinary \(m+3\)-point barycentric reduction can therefore send a positive essentiality polynomial to zero. Forcing finitely many witness values to retain positive mass is not justified at a boundary barycenter, and the frozen assumptions impose no faithfulness or minimum feature strength. Hidden-endogenous exogenization must additionally preserve actual functional dependencies rather than only a permitted latent projection.
open_obligations.attempted: The sourcewise reduction was augmented conceptually by all directed-feature indicators; those indicators are separately linear and can be preserved, but the two-copy source-feature polynomials remain nonlinear in the source being compressed. Retaining explicit witness pairs was also considered, but exact barycenter preservation with prescribed positive atoms does not follow on a proper face of the moment convex hull. The positive XOR support-deletion family confirms this failure of the naive route, although its illegal boundary has an equal-moment legal lift and hence is not a negative certificate. The compelled-collider test was solved only for an isolated selection root, as recorded in the partial result.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The mandatory collider test closes for the following nontrivial subcase.  Let \(V=\{X,Y,Z\}\) be binary, let the retained structural graph be \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\) with \(S\) an independent selection root, take \(B=\{X\}\), and assume the positive selected law \(q\) obeys the collider Markov restriction \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\).  Put
\[
 p_{xy}=q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y=y)\in(0,1).
\]
Choose independent \(U_X,U_Y\) with laws \(q_X,q_Y\), an independent \(U_Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and measurable sets \(E_{xy}\subset[0,1]\) with Lebesgue measure \(p_{xy}\).  The four sets can be chosen so that \(E_{0y}\ne E_{1y}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(y\), and \(E_{x0}\ne E_{x1}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(x\): begin with intervals of the prescribed lengths, and whenever an equality remains, exchange two sufficiently short subintervals between the set and its complement.  Positivity \(0<p_{xy}<1\) makes each such exchange possible, and finitely many disjoint exchanges preserve distinctions already installed.  Define
\[
 X=U_X,\qquad Y=U_Y,\qquad
 Z=\mathbf 1\{U_Z\in E_{XY}\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Pr(X=x,Y=y,Z=z)=q_X(x)q_Y(y)q(z\mid x,y)=q(x,y,z),
\]
and the two strict symmetric differences make both arrows into \(Z\) actual functional dependencies, even when \(q\) is unfaithful to one or both arrows.  Taking an independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), with \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\), gives \(c_v=\rho q(v)\) and \(d=\rho\).  For every bounded binary outcome map \(h\), truncated factorization gives the single attainable selected-intervention value
\[
 \theta=
 \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}q_Y(y)
 \bigl[h(0)(1-p_{by})+h(1)p_{by}\bigr].
\]
It is attained by the exact collider construction above.  Thus the exact-graph fiber and all its support-stratum closure points lift in this isolated-selection compelled-collider case.  This does not cover selected MAGs in which \(S\) has parents or latent ancestors, nor does it preserve an arbitrary pair \((n,d)\) beyond the value fixed by this collider factorization.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(I_b=\{v\in\Omega_V:B(v)=b\}\), and let \(M\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  By \(\text{ass:intervention-selection-margin}\) and \(\delta>0\),
\[
d_M\geq\delta>0,
\]
so every division below is legitimate.  Recursiveness gives a unique solution under each hard intervention.  Hence the definition of the hard-intervention submodel gives consistency: on the factual event \(\{V=v,S=1\}\) with \(v\in I_b\), replacing the already realized value \(B=b\) by \(do(B=b)\) leaves the recursive solution unchanged.  In particular, on that event,
\[
A^b=A(v),\qquad S^b=1.
\]
Since \(h(A^b)-h_-\geq0\), the disjoint factual events indexed by \(I_b\), \(\text{ass:selected-law-fit}\), and \(\text{ass:population-selection-margin}\) therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_M-h_-d_M
&=\mathbb E_M\!\left[(h(A^b)-h_-)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}\right]\\
&\geq\sum_{v\in I_b}(h(A(v))-h_-)\Pr_M(V=v,S=1)\\
&=\rho\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h(A(v))-h_-)\\
&\geq\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h(A(v))-h_-).
\end{aligned}
\]
Also \(d_M\leq1\).  The sum in the last display is nonnegative, so division by \(d_M\) yields
\[
\theta(M)-h_-=\frac{n_M-h_-d_M}{d_M}
\geq \frac{\delta}{d_M}\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h(A(v))-h_-)
\geq\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h(A(v))-h_-).
\]
Thus \(\theta(M)\geq L_\delta\), with \(L_\delta\) as in \(\text{def:saturated-envelope}\).  Applying exactly the same argument to the nonnegative outcome \(h_+-h\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_+d_M-n_M
&=\mathbb E_M\!\left[(h_+-h(A^b))\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}\right]\\
&\geq\rho\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h_+-h(A(v)))\\
&\geq\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h_+-h(A(v))),
\end{aligned}
\]
and hence
\[
\theta(M)\leq h_+-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h_+-h(A(v)))=U_\delta.
\]
This proves \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\subseteq[L_\delta,U_\delta]\).

We next construct legal endpoint models.  Finiteness of \(\Omega_A\) supplies states \(a_-\) and \(a_+\) satisfying \(h(a_-)=h_-\) and \(h(a_+)=h_+\).  Since \(|\Omega_B|\geq2\), fix \(b^\dagger\neq b\).  Introduce one exogenous source \(U\).  For every \(v\in\Omega_V\), give \(U\) a state \(u_v\) of mass
\[
\Pr(U=u_v)=\delta q(v).
\]
If \(\delta<1\), add a state \(u_0\) of mass \(1-\delta\); when \(\delta=1\), omit this zero-mass state.  All displayed masses are positive and there are at most \(m+1\) of them.

Use the recursive order consisting of \(B\) first and then \(V\setminus B\) and \(S\).  Set \(B(u_v)=B(v)\) and \(B(u_0)=b^\dagger\).  For each \(X\in V\setminus B\), complete a table \(X=f_X(B,U)\) so that
\[
f_X(B(v),u_v)=X(v).
\]
Set \(S(B(v),u_v)=1\), set \(S(b^\dagger,u_0)=0\) when \(u_0\) is present, and set
\[
S(b,u)=1\quad\text{for every positive-mass state }u.
\]
For the lower model, complete the coordinates of the \(A\)-table at intervention input \(b\) by
\[
A(b,u_v)=
\begin{cases}
A(v),&B(v)=b,\\
a_-,&B(v)\neq b,
\end{cases}
\qquad A(b,u_0)=a_-;
\]
for the upper model replace every displayed \(a_-\) by \(a_+\).  These prescriptions do not conflict with the factual table entries because \(b^\dagger\neq b\); all entries not yet specified may be filled arbitrarily.  This is a recursive SCM with a single exogenous source.

In either endpoint model, exactly the \(u_v\)-types are factually selected.  Consequently
\[
\Pr(V=v,S=1)=\delta q(v),\qquad \rho=\Pr(S=1)=\delta.
\]
Under \(do(B=b)\), every positive-mass type is selected, so \(d_M=1\geq\delta\).  Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_M^{(-)}
&=\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)h(A(v))
+\left(1-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\right)h_-\\
&=h_-+\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h(A(v))-h_-)=L_\delta,
\end{aligned}
\]
and similarly
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_M^{(+)}
&=\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)h(A(v))
+\left(1-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\right)h_+\\
&=h_+-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)(h_+-h(A(v)))=U_\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(d_M=1\), these are also the two values of \(\theta(M)\).

It remains to verify the exact graph restriction rather than merely a permitted graph.  By \(\text{ass:positive-selected-law}\), every \(u_v\) has positive mass.  For each coordinate \(X\in V\), the hypothesis that its state space has at least two elements and positivity of every joint cell provide positive-mass states of \(U\) at which the table for \(X\) differs (with the endogenous input \(B\) held fixed when \(X\notin B\)).  Thus \(U\) is an actual essential parent of every observed vertex under the definition of \(G_S(M)\), not merely a formal parent slot.  For every distinct \(X,Y\in V\), the latent fork \(X\leftarrow U\rightarrow Y\) therefore induces an adjacency after retaining \(S\), latent projection, and selected-MAG projection.  The resulting selected MAG has complete observed skeleton.  A complete skeleton has no nonadjacent vertex pair and hence no nontrivial separation; it also has no discriminating path with nonadjacent endpoints.  Consequently its selected MAG is in the equivalence class represented by the complete all-circle COPAG.  Hence \(G_S(M)\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\), verifying \(\text{ass:exact-copag-stratum}\).  Both endpoint SCMs consequently belong to \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).

For any \(t\in[0,1]\), take disjointly labelled source states from the lower and upper constructions, with their masses multiplied by \(1-t\) and \(t\), respectively.  This is still a one-source recursive SCM; its factual selected cells remain \(\delta q(v)\), its intervention denominator remains one, and the same common-source argument gives exact complete-COPAG legality.  Linearity of expectation gives
\[
\theta(M_t)=(1-t)L_\delta+tU_\delta.
\]
Thus every point of \([L_\delta,U_\delta]\) is attained, and together with the universal inequalities this proves
\[
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=[L_\delta,U_\delta].
\]

If \(h\) is constant, then \(h_-=h_+\) and directly \(n_M=h_-d_M\), so every compatible model has \(\theta(M)=h_-\); the construction above proves nonemptiness, hence the fiber is \(\{h_-\}\).  Finally, if the intervention is vacuous, the intervention submodel equals the factual model.  Using \(\sum_vq(v)=1\) and \(\text{ass:selected-law-fit}\),
\[
d_M=\Pr(S=1)=\sum_v c_v(M)=\rho,
\qquad
n_M=\sum_v h(A(v))c_v(M)=\rho\sum_vq(v)h(A(v)).
\]
Since \(\rho\geq\delta>0\), division gives \(\theta(M)=\sum_vq(v)h(A(v))\).  For nonemptiness, take one source with states \(u_v\) of masses \(\delta q(v)\), together when \(\delta<1\) with a state \(u_0\) of mass \(1-\delta\).  Put \(V(u_v)=v\), \(S(u_v)=1\), and \(S(u_0)=0\), with \(V(u_0)\) arbitrary.  Then \(c_v=\delta q(v)\) and, because the intervention is vacuous, \(d_M=\rho=\delta\).  Positivity of \(q\) makes the common source an essential parent of every observed vertex, so the preceding complete-skeleton argument verifies graph legality.  Thus the vacuous-intervention fiber is exactly the asserted singleton.

For the binary outcome \(h^*(a)=a\), intervention \(b=0\), and \(\delta^*=1/4\), \(\text{def:saturated-envelope}\) gives
\[
L_{\delta^*}=\delta^*q^*(0,1)=\frac14\frac2{10}=\frac1{20},
\qquad
U_{\delta^*}=1-\delta^*q^*(0,0)=1-\frac14\frac1{10}=\frac{39}{40}.
\]
The hypotheses of \(\text{thm:saturated-closed-form}\) hold for \(\mathcal P^*\), so this calculation already proves sharpness of the interval.  We now exhibit the asserted five-type endpoint certificates.

Let a single exogenous source \(U\) have states \(u_1,\ldots,u_5\) with respective masses
\[
(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4,w_5)=\frac1{40}(1,2,3,4,30).
\]
In both models define
\[
(B(u_i))_{i=1}^5=(0,0,1,1,1),
\]
and define the two rows of the selection table by
\[
(S(0,u_i))_{i=1}^5=(1,1,1,1,1),
\qquad
(S(1,u_i))_{i=1}^5=(1,1,1,1,0).
\]
For the lower endpoint use
\[
(A(0,u_i))_{i=1}^5=(0,1,0,0,0),
\qquad
(A(1,u_i))_{i=1}^5=(0,1,0,1,0),
\]
whereas for the upper endpoint use
\[
(A(0,u_i))_{i=1}^5=(0,1,1,1,1),
\qquad
(A(1,u_i))_{i=1}^5=(0,1,0,1,0).
\]
The natural selected cells of \(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4\) are, respectively, \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), while \(u_5\) is naturally unselected.  Therefore
\[
\rho=\sum_{i=1}^4w_i=\frac14,
\qquad
\bigl(c_{00},c_{01},c_{10},c_{11}\bigr)=\frac1{40}(1,2,3,4)=\rho q^*.
\]
Under \(do(B=0)\), the first selection row shows that \(d_M=\sum_iw_i=1\) in both models.  The lower and upper numerators are
\[
n_M^{(-)}=w_2=\frac2{40}=\frac1{20},
\qquad
n_M^{(+)}=w_2+w_3+w_4+w_5=\frac{39}{40}.
\]
Because the denominators equal one, these are the corresponding intervention means.

Finally, \(U\) is an actual essential parent of \(B\), \(A\), and \(S\): the displayed positive-mass table rows vary with \(U\) for each vertex.  Hence the latent projection contains an adjacency between \(B\) and \(A\), and its two-vertex selected MAG is represented by the complete all-circle COPAG \(\mathcal P^*\).  Thus both five-type SCMs satisfy the exact graph restriction, completing the certificate.

Define the coverage events
\[
E_q=\{q\in C_n\},\qquad E_g=\{\mathcal P\in\Pi_n\}.
\]
The two assumed marginal guarantees and the elementary union bound imply
\[
\Pr(E_q\cap E_g)
=1-\Pr(E_q^c\cup E_g^c)
\geq1-\Pr(E_q^c)-\Pr(E_g^c)
\geq1-\alpha_q-\alpha_g.
\]
On \(E_q\cap E_g\), the particular pair \((\mathcal P,q)\) occurs among the pairs indexing the union in \(\text{def:confidence-fiber}\).  Therefore, pointwise on this event,
\[
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)
\subseteq
\bigcup_{\mathcal P'\in\Pi_n,\,q'\in C_n}
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P',q')
\subseteq
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}
\bigcup_{\mathcal P'\in\Pi_n,\,q'\in C_n}
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P',q')
=\widehat{\mathfrak C}_n.
\]
Taking probabilities proves
\[
\Pr\!\left(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak C}_n\right)
\geq1-\alpha_q-\alpha_g.
\]
The argument uses only event inclusion; in particular, no differentiability, compactness, attainment, or uniqueness of an optimizer has entered.

For the saturated binary configuration, write \(q_{ij}=q(B=i,A=j)\).  By \(\text{thm:saturated-closed-form}\), with \(b=0\) and \(h(a)=a\),
\[
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=[\delta q_{01},\,1-\delta q_{00}].
\]
Under the declared i.i.d. sampling law, each cell count has its corresponding binomial marginal distribution.  Because \(l_{01}\) and \(l_{00}\) are one-sided exact lower confidence limits with error allocation \(\alpha_q/2\), their defining coverage properties are
\[
\Pr(l_{01}\leq q_{01})\geq1-\frac{\alpha_q}{2},
\qquad
\Pr(l_{00}\leq q_{00})\geq1-\frac{\alpha_q}{2}.
\]
No independence between these two limits is required.  A second application of the union bound gives
\[
\Pr(l_{01}\leq q_{01},\ l_{00}\leq q_{00})\geq1-\alpha_q.
\]
On this simultaneous event, \(\delta>0\) gives
\[
\delta l_{01}\leq\delta q_{01},
\qquad
1-\delta q_{00}\leq1-\delta l_{00},
\]
and hence
\[
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)
=[\delta q_{01},1-\delta q_{00}]
\subseteq[\delta l_{01},1-\delta l_{00}].
\]
Thus the reported finite-sample interval covers the entire sharp fiber with probability at least \(1-\alpha_q\), as claimed.

Let \(V=\{X,Y\}\), with \(\Omega_X=\Omega_Y=\{0,1\}\), let \(A=\{Y\}\), let \(B=\{X\}\), take \(b=0\), and define the bounded rational outcome map by \(h(y)=y\).  Let \(\mathcal P\) be the saturated two-vertex COPAG whose represented class contains the MAG \(G^{\leftrightarrow}\) having the single edge \(X\leftrightarrow Y\).  The selection vertex introduced below is isolated, so selection projection neither creates nor removes this edge.

For each \(t\in[0,1]\), define a finite recursive SCM \(M_t\) using four exogenous sources \(U,E_X,E_Y,E_S\).  They are mutually independent, with
\[
 U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(t),\qquad
 E_X,E_Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\qquad
 E_S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4).
\]
Here \(U\) is a source shared by \(X\) and \(Y\), whereas each of \(E_X,E_Y,E_S\) has only its correspondingly subscripted child.  The structural equations are
\[
 X=E_X\oplus U,\qquad Y=E_Y\oplus U,\qquad S=E_S,
\]
where \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two.  These equations are acyclic and all endogenous and exogenous state spaces are finite.

Fix \((x,y)\in\{0,1\}^2\).  For either \(u\in\{0,1\}\), independence and fairness of \(E_X,E_Y\) give
\[
 \Pr_{M_t}(X=x,Y=y\mid U=u)
 =\Pr(E_X=x\oplus u)\Pr(E_Y=y\oplus u)
 =\frac14.
\]
Averaging over \(U\) therefore gives \(\Pr_{M_t}(X=x,Y=y)=1/4\) for every \(t\).  Since \(S=E_S\) is independent of \((U,E_X,E_Y)\),
\[
 c_{(x,y)}(M_t)
 =\Pr_{M_t}(X=x,Y=y,S=1)
 =\frac14\cdot\frac14=\frac1{16}.
\]
Consequently \(\rho:=\Pr_{M_t}(S=1)=1/4\), and the selected law is
\[
 q(x,y)=\Pr_{M_t}(X=x,Y=y\mid S=1)
 =\frac{c_{(x,y)}(M_t)}{\rho}=\frac14.
\]
Thus \(q\) is rational and strictly positive on all four cells.

Under \(do(X=0)\), consistency of the recursive structural intervention leaves the equations for \(Y\) and \(S\) unchanged.  Hence \(Y^0=E_Y\oplus U\) and \(S^0=E_S\).  Conditional on either value of \(U\), \(Y^0\) is fair, and it is independent of \(S^0\).  It follows that
\[
 d_{M_t}=\Pr_{M_t}(S^0=1)=\frac14
\]
and
\[
 n_{M_t}
 =\mathbb E_{M_t}\!\left[h(Y^0)\mathbf 1\{S^0=1\}\right]
 =\Pr_{M_t}(Y^0=1,S^0=1)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac18.
\]
By the definition of the moment map,
\[
 \zeta(M_t)=\left(\left(\frac1{16}\right)_{(x,y)\in\{0,1\}^2},\frac18,\frac14\right)
\]
for every \(t\in[0,1]\).

It remains to compare exact graphs.  Suppose \(0<t<1\).  Both values of \(U\) then have positive probability.  For every value \(e_X\) of \(E_X\), the two source inputs give
\[
 e_X\oplus0\ne e_X\oplus1,
\]
and the same comparison holds for the table of \(Y\) at every \(e_Y\).  Thus, in the terminology of the exact graph-legality stratum, the common-source essential-feature polynomials for the incidences \(U\to X\) and \(U\to Y\) are strictly positive.  There is no directed functional dependence among \(X,Y,S\), and the private sources have no second child.  Latent projection of the shared essential source therefore gives exactly \(X\leftrightarrow Y\), with \(S\) isolated.  Hence \(G_S(M_t)=G^{\leftrightarrow}\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) for \(0<t<1\).

At \(t=0\), only \(U=0\) has positive probability, and at \(t=1\), only \(U=1\) has positive probability.  At either endpoint there do not exist two positive-mass values of the shared source to witness a change in either response table.  The common-source incidence polynomials in the exact graph-legality definition are therefore zero.  After removal of this null-set functional dependence, \(X\), \(Y\), and \(S\) have only mutually independent private sources, so \(G_S(M_0)\) and \(G_S(M_1)\) contain no \(X\)--\(Y\) edge.  In particular, both endpoint SCMs lose the bidirected edge present throughout \(0<t<1\), even though their moment vectors equal every interior moment vector.

Finally, the boundary vector has a graph-legal lift: \(M_{1/2}\) is distinct from both endpoint SCMs, satisfies \(G_S(M_{1/2})=G^{\leftrightarrow}\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\), and the displayed moment calculation gives
\[
 \zeta(M_{1/2})=\zeta(M_0)=\zeta(M_1).
\]
This proves both the claimed failure of moment preservation to preserve exact graph legality and the existence of a distinct legal representative of the same boundary moment vector.
